frequency_question: How often do major omnibus structural reform bills successfully clear both chambers and get signed into law under divided government within a single congressional session?
membership_rule: Includes major bipartisan energy, transportation, or regulatory reform packages (e.g., FAST Act, Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, Energy Policy Act). Excludes routine appropriations, single-issue non-controversial bills, and budget reconciliations.

cases.name: Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007
Mountain Valley Pipeline permitting rider (Debt Limit deal)

provenance_note: 7 cases named, 11 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.6x)
coverage_note: 7 named hits out of 11 major omnibus infrastructure/energy legislative vehicles attempted under divided government since 1995; 4 notable stalls/misses (e.g., 2010 cap-and-trade/energy bill failure, 2022 Manchin permitting reform collapse).
known_gaps: Excludes minor standalone pipeline approvals that bypass omnibus vehicle requirements.
skeleton: Total major bipartisan infrastructure/energy reform attempts with substantive permitting or interstate provisions in divided government eras since 1995
multiplier: 7 hits out of 11 major attempts identified in modern divided/polarized congresses
validity_reason: The baseline of polarized legislative bargaining and reliance on omnibus packages remains stable through current political eras.
